questions.question: Is there only one way to get saved?
answer: Yes. Salvation is only by the grace of God through faith in Jesus Christ. No person can be saved by works, religion, or personal effort. Jesus Christ alone paid the full penalty for sin through His death on the cross and offers eternal life as a free gift to those who believe in Him.
detail: YES. You can only be saved by grace through faith in Jesus Christ. Nothing more and nothing less. He is the only way to forgiveness of sin and everlasting life. He paid the penalty for your sin when he shed His perfect sinless blood and died on the Cross for our sins. “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Romans 6:23

questions.question: Do other religions get saved the same way?
answer: No. Scripture teaches there are only two belief systems: salvation by human works or salvation by faith in Jesus Christ alone. Any system that depends on works, rituals, law‑keeping, or religion cannot save. Salvation is found only by trusting Christ’s finished work on the cross.
detail: No. It has been said that there are only “two” religions.

1. You are either “saved” (NOT really) by good works. That is, by what you do. Example: sacraments, baptism, what you eat, by your behaviour, by following Old Testament law (Commandments), by your religion, by your church, your giving, your sabbath day, what you eat etc. OR

2. by believing in Jesus Christ as the Saviour of the world (Son of God) and believing by faith in Him to have paid the price for your sin with His death on the cross.
“Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.”
This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.” Titus 3:5-8
We do good works NOT to get saved but because we are saved. We do good works because of the Holy Spirit that dwells within the Saved that convicts us and encourages us to do right.

Salvation is not about what we have done but in whom we trust and what He has done on the cross on our behalf, sacrificed Himself with his death to pay for our sins. He who has not sinned dying for the sins of all mankind.

questions.question: Do I get saved by simply calling on Jesus Christ and asking Him to save me?
answer: Yes. When a person sincerely calls upon Jesus Christ in faith, trusting Him alone for salvation and turning from former beliefs, God saves them immediately. Salvation occurs at the moment of faith, not through repeated prayers or lifelong effort.
detail: YES! By sincerely trusting Jesus Christ the Son of God to save you, discarding whatever you previously believed was going to give you eternal life (This is  repentance: ‘a change of heart/mind’) and believing the Word of God and calling on the name of the Lord Jesus Christ to save you.  “For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.” Romans 10:13

questions.question: What is the Gospel?
answer: The Gospel is the good news that Jesus Christ died for our sins, was buried, and rose again the third day according to the Scriptures. This message is the power of God unto salvation for all who believe.
detail:
The Gospel refers to the death, burial, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. 
“Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand; By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain.”

For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures: And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles. And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.” I Corinthians 15:1-8

questions.question: Why do I need to be saved?
answer: Every person is born a sinner, spiritually dead, condemned already, and facing eternal separation from God. Salvation is necessary because only through Jesus Christ can sins be forgiven and eternal life received.
detail:
Because according to the scriptures:
      You are dead (spiritually) in trespasses and sins - Ephesians 2:1
      You are condemned - John 3:18
      You have the wrath of God abiding on you - John 3:36
      You are a servant of sin - Romans 6:17
      You are heading for the Lake of Fire - Revelation 20:15

B.  And God has promised you:	
      The gift of eternal life - Romans 6:23
      The forgiveness of sins - Colossians 1:14
      Salvation brought through His grace - Titus 2:11, Ephesians 2:8,9
      To dwell in your heart - Ephesians 3:17, John 14:23
      The love of Christ which passeth knowledge – Ephesians 3:19
      The joy of Jesus Christ – John 15:11
      The peace of God which passeth all understanding – Philippians 4:7

questions.question: Who is a Child of God?
answer: A Child of God is someone who has personally received Jesus Christ as Savior by faith. At the moment of salvation, the believer is born again spiritually and adopted into God’s family forever.
detail:
Someone who has received Jesus Christ as their personal Saviour by calling on Christ to be saved. 
“But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:” John 1:12 KJB
“For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.”  Romans 10:13 KJB

The moment you are saved you are adopted into God’s family, BORN AGAIN. 
“Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.” John 3:3-7. KJB

questions.question: If I have gone to church all my life but never personally trusted Christ, am I saved?
answer: No. Church attendance, family background, or religious activity cannot save anyone. Each individual must personally believe on Jesus Christ and call upon Him for salvation to become a born‑again Christian.
detail: No. You need to have personally trusted Jesus Christ as your Saviour by calling upon His name, believing that He is the Son of God, that He died for your sins, was buried for 3 days and then rose from the dead.  Romans 10:13

Neither your parents, your church, your family, your friends or your pastor or priest can save you by praying for you. Only believing and receiving Jesus Christ by faith personally can save you.  This is how you become a Child of God, a Born Again Christian. You are born once physically and when you become a Child of God you are born again spiritually, that is, adopted into God’s family.

It doesn’t matter what family, tribe, nationality, religion, colour, race, or economic status you belong to, you can only become a Child of God, a born again Christian, by believing and receiving Jesus Christ as your personal Saviour. He is our ONLY hope of Salvation, the ONLY begotten Son of God who became sin for us.
“For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be   made the righteousness of God in him.” 2 Corinthians 5:21 KJB

questions.question: How long does it take to get saved?
answer: Salvation is not a process but a single event that occurs instantly when a person believes on Jesus Christ. At that moment, the believer is saved, forgiven, and eternally secure, just as physical birth happens at a specific moment.
detail:
Salvation is NOT a process, it is an event. It is like marriage. When you say “I do” you are married. When you were physically born the doctor noted the date and time and that is your physical birthday.  When you call on Jesus Christ by faith through prayer and you receive Him as your personal Saviour that is the moment you become a Child of God and are adopted into the family of God, Born Again.  This is your spiritual birthday.  
‘Salvation’ being a ‘process’ comes from a false works based doctrine. Usually because of a misunderstanding of the context.  For example, in Philippians 2:12 Paul the Apostle says “work out your own salvation with fear and trembling” but he is NOT talking to the unsaved about how to get saved, but rather talking to the saved on how to behave once you are saved. He is talking to those who are already born again Christians and encouraging them to behave in a Christ like manner.

questions.question: What is Assurance of Salvation?
answer: Assurance of salvation is the confidence and certainty that a believer knows they possess eternal life because they have trusted Jesus Christ. This assurance is based on God’s promises, not feelings or performance.
detail: “Assurance of salvation” means you have intellectual and spiritual certainty that you are saved and belong to God, that you possess eternal life, Salvation.
In II Timothy 1:12b “ … for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day.”

“And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life. These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.” 1 John 5:11–13

questions.question: Why do I need Assurance of Salvation?
answer: Assurance brings joy, confidence, comfort, and spiritual stability in the Christian life. Knowing one’s salvation is secure allows believers to grow, serve God faithfully, and stand firm in truth.
detail:
Assurance brings us JOY - I John 1:4
     Assurance brings us CONFIDENCE before God – 1 John 3:19,21
     Assurance brings us COMFORT of Heart – Colossians 2:2
     Assurance brings us STABILITY – James 1:8

questions.question: How can I be sure I am saved?
answer: A believer can be sure of salvation because God cannot lie, His promises are certain, and the Holy Spirit bears witness through the Word of God. Evidence of salvation includes faith in Christ, love for other believers, obedience to God’s Word, and spiritual fruit.
detail: 1. Because of who God is:
“In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began”.– Titus 1:2.  OUR GOD WHO CANNOT LIE SAID IT – THAT SETTLES IT!
2. Because of what God Promised:

God says I HAVE everlasting life, and I SHALL NOT come into condemnation                                                                      John 5:24.
God says He will in NO WISE cast you out.  John 6:37   
God says those who call on the name of the Lord SHALL be saved. Rom.10:13
3. Because I know:

I BELIEVED on the Lord Jesus Christ - Acts 16:31
I HAVE the Son - 1John 5:12
I have a love for the BRETHREN - 1 John 3:14
I desire to keep God’s COMMANDMENTS - 1 John 2:3
I desire to turn from the WORLD and all its sin - 1 John 2:15
I am OVERCOMING the World – 1 John 5:4
I have the WITNESS of the Spirit within through the Word –  ‘He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.- 1 John 5:10
My life is evidencing good FRUIT Matthew 7:17,18
I hear the Lord’s VOICE through the Word of God and desire to follow Him – John 10:27
These things are evidence that a person is saved.

title: Eternal Security / Security Of The Believer

questions.question: What is Eternal Security?
answer: Eternal security is the biblical truth that a person who is genuinely saved by faith in Jesus Christ is saved forever and cannot lose their salvation. Salvation is kept by God’s power, not by human effort, because it rests on Christ’s finished work and God’s unchanging promise.

questions.question: Does Baptism save me?
answer: No. According to the Bible, baptism always follows salvation because it is an act of obedience, not a means of salvation. A person is saved by grace through faith in Jesus Christ alone, and baptism comes afterward as a public testimony of that salvation. Baptism pictures what has already taken place spiritually: the believer’s identification with the death, burial, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Because salvation is complete at the moment of faith, baptism cannot add to or complete salvation but instead declares openly that a person has trusted Christ and is now walking in obedience to Him.

questions.question: Why is the Bible important?
answer: The Bible is God’s inspired, preserved, and authoritative Word, given to reveal truth, provide doctrine, correct error, and guide believers in righteousness. It is the final authority for faith and practice and must be believed and obeyed.

questions.question: What is prayer?
answer: Prayer is communication with God through Jesus Christ, in which believers speak to God in faith, dependence, and obedience. Prayer includes praise, confession, thanksgiving, and requests, and is essential for spiritual growth and fellowship with God.

questions.question: Who is God?
answer: God is the eternal, holy, all‑powerful Creator of all things, existing as one God in three persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. He is perfect in truth, love, justice, and mercy, and is worthy of all worship and obedience.

questions.question: Who is Jesus Christ?
answer: Jesus Christ is the eternal Son of God who became man, lived a sinless life, died on the cross for our sins, and rose again bodily. He is the only Savior and the only mediator between God and man.

questions.question: Who is the Holy Spirit?
answer: The Holy Spirit is God, the third person of the Trinity, who convicts the world of sin, regenerates believers at salvation, indwells them permanently, and empowers them to live a godly life.

questions.question: What is the fruit of the Spirit?
answer: The fruit of the Spirit is the visible evidence of the Holy Spirit’s work in the life of a believer. According to the Bible, when a person is saved and walks in obedience to the Holy Spirit, God produces Christ‑like character within them. This fruit is not something believers create through their own effort, but the natural result of abiding in Christ and yielding to the Spirit’s leading. The fruit of the Spirit reflects the character of Jesus Christ and demonstrates spiritual maturity and a transformed life.
The Bible identifies the fruit of the Spirit as: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, and temperance: against such there is no law.

questions.question: What is Heaven?
answer: Heaven is the eternal dwelling place of God and all who are saved through faith in Jesus Christ. It is a place of joy, peace, and everlasting fellowship with God, free from sin, sorrow, and death.

questions.question: What is Hell and the Lake of Fire?
answer: Hell and the Lake of Fire are real places of eternal punishment prepared for Satan and those who reject Jesus Christ. It is a place of conscious separation from God and is the final destiny of the unsaved.

questions.question: Who is Satan?
answer: Satan is a real created being who rebelled against God and now seeks to deceive and destroy. Though powerful, he is limited by God and will ultimately be judged and defeated forever.

questions.question: What are angels?
answer: Angels are created spiritual beings who serve God and minister according to His will. They are not to be worshipped and always act in obedience to God’s commands.

questions.question: What is false doctrine?
answer: False doctrine is any teaching that contradicts or adds to God’s Word, often leading people away from the truth of the Gospel. Believers are commanded to test all teaching by Scripture.

questions.question: How can false teachers be identified?
answer: False teachers often deny biblical truth, exalt themselves, or promote works‑based salvation. Scripture warns believers to be vigilant and to judge teaching by God’s Word.

questions.question: Will Jesus Christ return?
answer: Yes. Jesus Christ will return bodily and visibly as promised in Scripture. His return will bring judgment and the fulfilment of God’s plan for the ages.

questions.question: What is repentance?
answer: Repentance is a change of mind that results in turning to God and trusting Jesus Christ alone for salvation. It is not turning from sin to be saved, but turning from unbelief to faith in Christ.

questions.question: What is soul winning?
answer: Soul winning is sharing the Gospel of Jesus Christ so that others may hear, believe, and be saved. Every believer is called to be a witness for Christ.

questions.question: What is discipleship?
answer: Discipleship is the process of spiritual growth in which a saved believer learns God’s Word, follows Christ obediently, and matures in faith through teaching, fellowship, and service, becoming more like Christ.

questions.question: What is a statement of faith?
answer: A statement of faith is a clear summary of what a believer or church holds to be true according to the Bible. It defines core doctrines such as salvation, the nature of God, the authority of Scripture, and the Gospel, helping guard against error and false teaching.

questions.question: What are the ordinances of the church?
answer: The two ordinances given by Christ to the local church are baptism and the Lord’s Supper. These ordinances do not save but are acts of obedience that picture Gospel truths and are to be observed by believers.

questions.question: Should Christians give financially?
answer: Yes. Giving is an act of worship and obedience for believers, done willingly and cheerfully, not to earn salvation but as a response to God’s grace and provision. To tithe is a command, offerings are a gift to God as a show of love and appreciation and alms is a gift to the poor and a blessing to God.

questions.question: Why is the local church important?
answer: The local church is God’s design for worship, teaching, fellowship, accountability, and service. Believers are commanded not to forsake assembling together, as the church strengthens faith and unity.

questions.question: What does the Bible teach about marriage and purity?
answer: Marriage is a sacred covenant ordained by God between one man and one woman, and believers are called to live morally pure lives honouring God in body, mind, and conduct. God honours purity and obedience to His design.

questions.question: What authority governs the church?
answer: Jesus Christ is the head of the church, and the Bible is its final authority. Church leaders are to serve under Christ, teaching and guiding according to Scripture, not personal authority.

questions.question: Will believers receive rewards for service?
answer: Yes. While salvation is a free gift, believers will be rewarded according to their faithful service to Christ. These rewards are given at the judgment seat of Christ.

questions.question: Why did Jesus teach in parables?
answer: Jesus used parables to reveal spiritual truth to those who believed while concealing truth from those who rejected Him. Parables illustrate God’s truth using real‑life examples. A parable is an earthly story with an heavenly meaning.
references: (See pages 59-65 ‘Answers Book – lists reasons for Christ speaking in parables, lists and explains some parables and how to interpret parables.)

questions.question: How do you tell the difference between a parable and a true story in the Bible?
answer: The Bible distinguishes parables from true stories by context, language, and purpose. Parables are teaching illustrations used by Jesus to convey spiritual truth, often introduced as a parable and using symbolic or representative characters to teach one main lesson. True stories, by contrast, are presented as historical accounts involving real people, places, and events, without symbolic explanation, and are recorded as factual occurrences. Jesus clearly identified when He spoke in parables, while true stories—such as historical narratives or specific accounts—are presented plainly as actual events. Careful attention to context and Scripture allows believers to rightly divide between illustrative teaching and literal history.

questions.question: Why should Christians study the Bible regularly?
answer: Studying God’s Word strengthens faith, provides wisdom, guards against false doctrine, and equips believers to live obedient and fruitful lives.

questions.question: How should believers respond to pastors and false prophets?
answer: The Bible teaches that pastors are God‑appointed shepherds who are called to feed, guide, and care for God’s people through faithful teaching of the Scriptures and godly example. Believers are instructed to respect, pray for, and submit to biblical leadership as pastors follow Christ and teach according to God’s Word. At the same time, Scripture gives strong warnings about false prophets and teachers who distort truth, deny sound doctrine, or promote themselves rather than Christ. Believers are commanded to test all teaching by the Word of God, to reject any message that contradicts the Gospel, and to separate from those who persist in false doctrine. Discernment, grounded in Scripture, protects the church and keeps believers firmly established in truth.

questions.question: How can I know God’s will for my life?
answer: God reveals His will through His Word, prayer, and obedience. As believers yield themselves fully to God and renew their minds through Scripture, He faithfully directs their paths according to His purpose and timing.

questions.question: Does God call every believer to serve Him?
answer: Yes. Every believer is called by God to serve Him in some capacity. While callings differ in function, all believers are gifted by God and called to serve for His glory and the edification of others as part of the body of Christ.

questions.question: What is the difference between joy and happiness?
answer: Happiness depends on circumstances, while joy is an inward, spiritual condition produced by the Holy Spirit and rooted in a relationship with God, remaining even in trials.

questions.question: What does “quickened” mean in the Bible context?
answer: In the Bible, the word “quickened” means to be made alive, specifically to be given spiritual life by God. It refers to God’s act of bringing a person who is spiritually dead in sin to spiritual life through Jesus Christ. Before salvation, a person is described as spiritually dead, separated from God because of sin. When someone is saved, God quickens them by the power of the Holy Spirit, giving them new life, new nature, and the ability to know, love, and serve God. In Scripture, “quickened” is never about physical speed or emotion, but about spiritual resurrection and regeneration.

title: What Is Spiritual Warfare And How Does It Affect Me?

questions.question: What is spiritual warfare and how does it affect believers?
answer: Spiritual warfare is the ongoing conflict between God’s truth and Satan’s deception, affecting believers as they seek to live godly lives. God provides spiritual armour and victory through faith and obedience to His Word.

title: King James Bible vs New Versions

questions.question: Why do you use the King James Bible?
answer: The King James Bible is used because it is believed to be a faithful, accurate, and preserved translation of God’s Word based on the traditional Hebrew and Greek texts. Many newer Bible versions rely on different manuscripts and often remove, alter, or weaken key words, verses, and doctrines found in the King James Bible. Scripture teaches that God has promised to preserve His Word, and believers who use the King James Bible trust it as the final authority for faith and practice without continual revision or doctrinal confusion. Using one preserved standard helps guard against error and provides consistency in doctrine, teaching, and memorisation.

questions.question: What BIBLE verses show that the Bible is inerrant, eternal, and unchanging?
answer: The Bible teaches that God’s Word is perfect, inspired by God, eternal, and preserved forever. Scripture declares that God’s Word does not change with time, culture, or human opinion and will endure beyond heaven and earth. Because God Himself is unchanging, His Word remains authoritative, true, and reliable for every generation. These verses show that the Bible is without error, preserved by God, and eternally settled.
references: Psalm 12:6–7 – “The words of the LORD are pure words… Thou shalt keep them, O LORD, thou shalt preserve them from this generation for ever.”
Psalm 119:89 – “For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.”

Matthew 24:35 – “Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.”
Matthew 5:18 – “Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law…”
2 Timothy 3:16 – “All scripture is given by inspiration of God…”
Psalm 119:160 – “Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever.”
1 Peter 1:25 – “But the word of the Lord endureth for ever.”
